hook_text: Half a term of ropes, teeth and clicks fits in two counting rules and three verbs. Revision in a minute.
clip_script: Pulleys: count the ropes holding the load up. That is your advantage. Pull that many times the rope. Measured comes out a bit less; call it efficiency. Controls: none of them adds force. The ratchet allows one way. The brake stops, turning motion into heat. The cleat holds a rope and lets go in a second. Gears: count teeth, driven over driver. Small driving big is slow and strong. The idler flips direction only. Bevel turns a corner. Rack makes a straight line. Worm gives a huge reduction and locks itself. Avoid the four traps: hand rope counted, control said to add force, ratio upside down, idler blamed for the ratio.
visual_style: Whiteboard split in three: a tackle with ropes numbered; three icons for ratchet, brake, cleat with the verbs; a gear train with tooth counts and the ratio; four red crosses for the traps.
mood: Brisk and confident, like the last page of revision notes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the two rules and three verbs on one card for the exam.
